title: Mirabel and the Songbook
premise: Silas Lockridge, a wedding planner who quietly stopped believing in love after vanishing from their own engagement eleven years ago, has built a careful life of small, safe steps. When a client's grandmother donates an old songbook to Silas's shop and a letter falls from its pages—postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to Silas in handwriting they'd know anywhere—they learn that Juniper Vale, the fiancée they abandoned, has been searching for them ever since, and that she is now gravely ill. Silas must return to the coastal town and the family they betrayed, risking exposure of why they ran: not cold feet, but a secret about their identity that Juniper's family made unbearable. In the climax, Silas performs the wedding of Juniper's niece using the songbook's music, publicly claiming their true self before the whole town; Juniper, frail but clear-eyed, chooses to spend whatever time remains with the person Silas actually is. The story ends not with a cure but with a vow renewed on borrowed time—love chosen freely, at last, against duty, grief, and fear.
about_author: August Vasquez is a former wedding violinist turned novelist who writes love stories for people who flinched the first time. They live in a converted chapel on the Oregon coast with a deaf old dog and an unreasonable number of sheet music collections.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Binding
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Ten years into a meticulous, invisible life running a wedding-planning studio, Silas takes on one last job for the Vale family—unaware at first whose family it is. While cataloguing a donated songbook, they find a letter postmarked eleven years ago in Juniper's handwriting. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine; the safe architecture of Silas's life cracks on the very first page.

chapters.title: What the Songbook Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Silas and Juniper, in flashback. Silas travels to the coastal town under a false client name and discovers Juniper is ill and has been leaving letters in books for years, hoping one would reach them. Flashbacks reveal the identity secret and family pressure that drove Silas away. The beat is aching tenderness tangled with guilt—two people circling the same wound from opposite sides.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, present day. Juniper confronts Silas in her garden, and the reunion detonates: fury, confession, and the truth Silas has never spoken aloud. Juniper's family demands Silas leave before the niece's wedding; duty, reputation, and Juniper's declining health stack against them. The emotional beat is raw confrontation—the whole heart finally offered, and refused, at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Last Song in the Book
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the wedding, with the family watching and Juniper too weak to stand long, Silas steps in when the musician fails—singing from the songbook and, in front of everyone, speaking their true name and their history with Juniper. Juniper chooses them publicly in return. The beat is catharsis and quiet resolution: no cure, no guarantee, but a vow made whole, on whatever time is left.
